Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle as the Indian players are seen in a huddle just inside the ropes. The Sri Lankan opening pair of Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka stride out to the middle as well. It will be skipper Hardik Pandya to get proceedings underway with the ball here.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, a mammoth total of 228 is what is on the board, and Sri Lanka will need a special performance from their batters. India will hope their bowlers to defend this one and win the series. Which team will get over the line? We shall find out together. Chase coming up shortly...

Suryakumar Yadav, the man of the moment comes up for a quick chat. He says that he is happy with the way his innings went after the captain elected to bat first. Adds that few shots are pre-determined but all the shots he plays are his own and is happy with it. Jokes that his form has gone with the new year and it is a new beginning in 2023 before stating that the outfield is lightning quick and that helps as well.

Sri Lanka's abysmal performance on the field has pushed them into a corner and now they will need a big stand from their openers. Kasun Rajitha was the only economical bowler, not so economical but in the context of how many runs were scored, he was better than the rest and he managed to bag one wicket, the rest of their bowlers leaked runs. They will need to put up a special performance now with the blade to chase this down. Dilshan Madushanka took two wickets whilst Chamika Karunaratne and Wanindu Hasaranga had one in their bank but none of them could keep the scoring rate down.

Suryakumar Yadav, take a bow! It was an exceptional display of batting from the Indian batters and they were all over the Sri Lankan bowlers. They lost Ishan Kishan early on but Gill and Rahul Tripathi went all over them. Once Rahul Tripathi was dismissed, Suryakumar Yadav came on with all guns blazing. He ran a havoc over the Lankan bowlers and was toying around with them playing shots all over the ground. The non-strikers lost wickets, playing short cameos, but Suryakumar Yadav had only one plan in mind - Bat, bat, and bat. He scored 112* runs off just 51 deliveries and made India reach a mammoth total of 228 runs.

FOUR! Suryakumar Yadav ends the Indian innings with a signature shot! This is bowled shorter and outside off, SKY uses his wrists to maneuver the ball and pull it over backward square leg for a boundary. India finish with a mammoth score of 228/5 on the board!

Well bowled! This is in the blockhole around off, Axar Patel hangs deep and looks to heave it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls toward backward point and they get a single.
Another slower one, shorter and around off, this is lofted down to long on for a single.
Swing and a miss! Slower one, bowled into the pitch and over the stumps. Suryakumar Yadav has a swipe across the line but is completely undone by the lack of pace.
SIX! Just a slap! Short and wide, Suryakumar Yadav advances and thumps it over the cover fence for a biggie. Double Nelson comes up now!
Nicely bowled! Slower one, on a good length and well outside off. Suryakumar Yadav looks to hit it hard and through covers but is beaten by the lack of pace.

FOUR! A poor delivery to end the over and 16 runs come off it. An attempted slower yorker turns out to be a juicy full toss around off. Axar Patel pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.

Goes full and wide, takes pace off as well. Suryakumar Yadav looks to open the face of the bat and carve it over point but gets a thick outside edge that flies down to third man on the bounce. A single is taken.
Slower one, full and on middle, this is heaved down to long on for a single.
FOUR! And again! Nails the wide yorker and Axar Patel yet again just throws his bat at it. The ball flies off the outside edge and over short third man for another boundary.
FOUR! Edged away! Fullish length wide of the off stump, Axar Patel goes hard at it and carves it over backward point for a boundary.
WIDE! Slower one, on a good length and angled way across the left-hander. Wided.

There it is, Suryakumar Yadav gets to a scintillating HUNDRED! What a player this guy is and he is showing no signs of stopping. This is a dipping full toss outside off, SKY drives it to sweeper cover and gets across for the single. He takes off the helmet and takes in the applause from the crowd, and to be fair, he has more than deserved it.

Top over from Maheesh Theekshana given the circumstances, just 6 runs off it. Full again and at the toes, this is flicked away through mid-wicket for only a single. The 200 is now up for India and Suryakumar Yadav moves to 99.
A rare dot ball! Full and around off, Suryakumar Yadav drives it toward extra cover.
Flatter one, on the pads, Suryakumar Yadav works it off the back foot toward wide long on and they race back for two. Excellent running.
Sri Lanka won't mind the singles at this stage. This is on a length and angling down leg, Patel tucks it away through mid-wicket for one.
This is fired in full and on the pads, Suryakumar Yadav drills it down to wide long on for a single.
This is quicker and flatter outside off, Axar Patel cuts it to deep backward point for one.
Another slower one, on a good length and on leg stump. Axar Patel eases it through mid on for one and despite the wicket, 16 runs come off that over.
FOUR! Starts from where he left off in the previous game. This is slower and shorter outside off, Axar Patel has all the time in the world to slap it away into the point fence.
Axar Patel walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man! A back of the hand slower ball from Dilshan Madushanka. This is on a length and outside off. Deepak Hooda looks to shuffle across and thump kit downtown but mistimes the shot. The ball travels flat and toward long on where Wanindu Hasaranga takes a good low catch. India keep on losing wickets at regular intervals and Sri Lanka will be a bit relieved.
Commentary.Howout: c Wanindu Hasaranga b Dilshan Madushanka

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on leg stump, this is pushed off the back foot down to long on for one.

FOUR! Suryakumar Yadav falls over and yet he manages to get the boundary, unreal stuff! Dilshan Madushanka serves it full and well outside off, SKY pre-meditates and shuffles a long way across before scooping the slower delivery over backward square leg for a boundary.

SIX! There is no stopping Suryakumar Yadav and he moves into the 90s. This is full and wide, angling across, SKY opens the face of the bat at the last moment and slices it away over the third-man fence for a maximum.
FOUR! Hammered away! This is dug in short and on the body, Deepak Hooda stays on the back foot and pulls it away into the square leg fence.
Deepak Hooda walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Hardik Pandya looks to up the ante but holes out. Kasun Rajitha pitches it up now on off stump and takes pace off the ball. Pandya tries to get under it and loft it over long off but mistimes it badly. The ball goes high and lands around long off where Dhananjaya de Silva takes a good catch. The Indian skipper departs and Sri Lanka get a timely wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Dhananjaya de Silva b Kasun Rajitha

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, full and outside off, Yadav drives it through covers for only a single.
SIX! Bread and butter for Suryakumar Yadav! Kasun Rajitha misses the yorker on leg stump and serves a low full toss, SKY gets across and scoops it all the way over fine leg for a maximum.
Length again and on the pads again as well, this is flicked away to deep backward square leg for one.
Good length angled into the pads, Hardik Pandya nudges it through square leg and races back for the second.
Nagging length around off, it is the wrong 'un. Suryakumar Yadav rocks back to cut but fails to beat the man at short third man.
Full and around off, driven down to long off for a single.
The skipper, Hardik Pandya walks in.

OUT! TIMBER! Wanindu Hasaranga gets his revenge but the damage is already done. Shubman Gill walks down the pitch and Hasaranga sees him coming. Hasaranga pulls the length back and bowls it flatter around middle. Gill gets beaten in the flight and ends up walking past the ball. The ball castles into middle stump and Gill departs after a solid knock.
Excellent running! A tad shorter and on the pads, Gill tucks it away through mid-wicket for a brace.
SIX! Clean strike! Drops it a bit short and it is the googly. Shubman Gill picks it up and rocks back before whacking it over the mid-wicket fence for a huge hit.
Leg bye! On a length and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav looks to fetch and sweep but misses. The ball comes off the body and rolls toward short third man. They get a leg bye.
FOUR! Shubman Gill gets into the act now and 23 runs come off that over, a huge one for India. This is bowled on a good length, Gill just stands tall and short-arm jabs it into the cow corner fence.
Fuller and on leg stump, this is pushed down to long on for one.
SIX! And again! This is a massacre now! Flighted up, full and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav goes inside-out and lofts it over the extra cover fence for back-to-back maximums.
SIX! High and handsome! This is tossed up on a length and around off, Suryakumar Yadav lofts it against the turn and smokes it over the extra cover fence for a biggie.

FOUR! Suryakumar Yadav is finding the gaps without any efforts out there. This is flatter and into the pads, SKY just plays a whippy shot and the ball goes perfectly in between the fielders at long and deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
This is quicker and around off, Suryakumar Yadav waits and taps it to the left of the man at deep point for a couple of runs.
Goes back to over the wicket and serves a fullish delivery around leg stump, this is flicked away behind square leg for only a single.

SIX! Effortlessly done! Shorter and on the body, looking to cramp up the batter. Suryakumar Yadav stays deep and whips it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie. 17 already off the over and there's still one ball left.

FOUR! A game of fine margins and Suryakumar Yadav brings up yet another fabulous FIFTY in T20Is! Dilshan Madushanka misses the yorker by a couple of inches and SKY thumps it over extra cover for a boundary. Can he take India to over 200 now?
Top comeback! Switches to around the wicket and nails the yorker around off stump. Suryakumar Yadav looks to dig it out but the ball sneaks under the willow.

SIX! WOW! Suryakumar Yadav is toying with the bowlers here. SKY pre-meditates and shuffles across the stumps, Dilshan Madushanka looks to follow him but ends up serving a full toss. SKY is able to play the falling scoop and the ball flies over the fine leg fence for a maximum.
Dilshan Madushanka starts off his new spell with a short ball over leg stump. Shubman Gill backs away and flat-bats it down to long on for a single.
Excellent work in the deep! Tossed up outside off, Suryakumar Yadav plays a lofted drive, inside-out over extra cover. The man from sweeper cover runs to his right and saves two runs for his side.
Bowls it quicker and flatter around off, Suryakumar Yadav is late on the cut but gets it behind square on the off side for a couple of runs.
Shorter and around leg, this is pulled off the back foot to deep mid-wicket for a single.
This is full and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav stylishly sweeps it using his wrists and down to deep backward square leg for one more.
Sees him coming and fires it on the pads, Gill works it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Wanindu Hasaranga comes back into the attack and starts off with a flatter delivery on leg stump. Shubman Gill goes on the back foot and eases it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Slower one, bowled into the pitch and well outside off. Shubman Gill plays a crossed-batted shot down to wide long on and picks up a run.
Good length on middle, Suryakumar Yadav works it off the back foot in front of mid-wicket for a single.

SIX! This is classic SKY! Full and straight, Suryakumar Yadav gets inside the line of the ball and scoops it off the stumps all the way over the fine leg fence for a maximum. The 50-run stand is also up between these two.
FOUR! Slapped away! Suryakumar Yadav advances and Chamika Karunaratne bangs it in halfway down the track. This is outside off and Yadav hits it up and over cover-point to find the fence.

Two dots in a row! This is nicely bowled by Chamika Karunaratne, shorter and around off. Suryakumar Yadav looks to get low and just ramp it over the keeper's head but is beaten due to the extra bounce.
On a fullish length and angling in from around off. Suryakumar Yadav drives it on the up but straight to mid off.

Drinks break! At the halfway mark and India are 92/2! After the early set-back, Rahul Tripathi did well to counter the Lankan bowlers and although he got out, Tripathi provided some much-needed momentum to the innings. Sri Lanka will feel they have failed to capitalize on the decent start and will be aware of the fact that Suryakumar Yadav is already on a roll. Wickets are the key here and the visitors need at least a couple of them quickly. An exciting phase of play awaits.
A low full toss, on off, Suryakumar Yadav lofts it towards long on for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, Suryakumar Yadav knocks it to long on for a brace.
Outside off this time, Shubman Gill guides it to deep point for one more.
Bowls it on off, turning away, Suryakumar Yadav eases it to left of mid off for one.
Fuller again, Shubman Gill knocks it to long on for one.
Bowls it fuller and on off, Suryakumar Yadav drives it towards long off for one.
Maheesh Theekshana (1-0-12-0) is back on.
On off this time, Suryakumar Yadav taps it to deep covers for one.
FOUR! Fine shot. Slightly shorter and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav rocks back and cuts it in the gap, and through backward point for a boundary!
Bowls it on off, Shubman Gill drills it towards long on for one.
Fuller and on off, Suryakumar Yadav sweeps it towards deep square leg for one.
Bowls it down leg, Suryakumar Yadav looks to flick it but gets a rap on his pads. A stifled appeal turned down.
Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill drills it to long on for one.
On a length and on off, Shubman Gill flicks it towards mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on off, Suryakumar Yadav drills it towards long on for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, Shubman Gill pulls it towards mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on off, Suryakumar Yadav drills it to long on for one.
SIX! Up and over. Slightly shorter and on off, Suryakumar Yadav hangs back and pulls it over backward square leg for a huge six. The crowd is chanting, SURYA, SURYA!
FOUR! Fine shot. Bowls it fuller and on off, Suryakumar Yadav drives it uppishly, over extra cover for a boundary!
SIX! All the way. Fuller and on middle, slower too. Shubman Gill reads it well and heaves it over cow corner for a maximum. Excellent timing on this!
Bowls it on middle, Suryakumar Yadav sweeps it towards square leg for one.
Fuller one, turning away, Shubman Gill flicks it to mid on for one.
Slightly shorter and on off, Suryakumar Yadav cuts it behind point for one.
Bowls it on off, Shubman Gill guides it to point for one.
Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill eases it to the man at covers.
On a length, with some extra bounce, Suryakumar Yadav defends it to the man at point.
Wanindu Hasaranga comes into the attack.
Wide! This one lands down leg, Suryakumar Yadav looks to tickle it but misses.
Suryakumar Yadav is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Chamika Karunaratne gets his man after conceding two sixes and gets the much-needed breakthrough for his side. Slightly shorter, with some extra bounce, and outside off, Rahul Tripathi looks to guide it but mistimes it completely. It carries towards Dilshan Madushanka at short third man who takes a good catch diving to his right.
Commentary.Howout: c Dilshan Madushanka b Chamika Karunaratne

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Action replay of the last delivery! Touch fuller and on off, Rahul Tripathi lofts it over long off for another biggie!
SIX! Fuller and on off, Rahul Tripathi uses his feet and lofts this with a straight bat and straight down the ground as well for a maximum!
Bowls it fuller and on middle and leg, Shubman Gill looks to drill it but gets an inside edge onto the pads as the ball rolls towards the off side. They cross.
Shorter and outside off, Shubman Gill looks to slap it but misses.
Chamika Karunaratne to have a bowl now.
FOUR! Fuller one and on off, Rahul Tripathi gets on a bit low and lofts it over bowler's head as the ball runs away into the fence in no time. Boundary!
Bowls it outside off, Rahul Tripathi looks to loft it but misses.
Bowls it on leg, Rahul Tripathi sweeps it but finds the man at backward square leg.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries. This is a tad shorter and on off stump, Rahul Tripathi shuffles across and drives it through covers for another boundary!
FOUR! Fuller and on off, Rahul Tripathi uses the pace of the ball and sweeps it through backward square leg for a boundary!
On a length and on leg, pace off. Rahul Tripathi blocks it back towards the bowler.
Maheesh Theekshana to have a bowl now.
Bowls it on middle, Rahul Tripathi knocks it to mid on for one.
Good-length delivery, shaping in, Shubman Gill looks to play at it but gets an inside edge as the ball rolls towards square leg. They cross.
On a length, with some extra bounce, angling in, Shubman Gill blocks it to short covers.
Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill dances down the track and slices it over covers for a brace.
Slightly shorter and on off, Shubman Gill taps it to the man at covers.
Bowls it on off, Rahul Tripathi guides it towards backward point for one.
FOUR! Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill clears his front foot and drives it through covers for a boundary. Excellent timing on this.
SIX! All the way. Fuller and on off, 137.8 kph. Shubman Gill hangs back and heaves it over long on for a biggie!
On a length and on off, Shubman Gill taps it to mid on. Dot.
This one lands on off, Rahul Tripathi opens the face of his bat and guides it towards deep backward point for one.

FOUR! Living by the sword. Fuller and on off, Rahul Tripathi shimmies down the wicket and looks to loft it, but gets a thick inside edge. The ball flies through the diving fielder at square leg and into the fence for a boundary. That would have been an unbelievable catch!
Bowls it fuller and on off, Rahul Tripathi eases it to short covers.
A maiden from Kasun Rajitha! On a length and on middle, Shubman Gill eases it to short mid-wicket.
On a length and on off, Shubman Gill flicks it to the man at mid-wicket.
Another one outside off, Shubman Gill taps it straight to the man at covers.
Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill defends it to short covers.
Similar to the last delivery, 126.1kph. Shubman Gill doesn't offer any stroke to it.
This one lands outside off, Shubman Gill leaves it alone.
Kasun Rajitha to bowl from the other end.

FOUR! This one lands down leg, Rahul Tripathi tickles it. The ball carries to the left of the keeper. He dives to his left but just gets his glove to it as the ball races away the fine leg fence for a boundary. Close call!
On a length and on middle, Rahul Tripathi blocks it solidly off the back foot.
Rahul Tripathi is in at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! An early breakthrough in the game for Sri Lanka and they are happy. Bowls it slightly shorter, shaping away from the left hander. Ishan Kishan gets in two minds and puts his bat at the very end, gets a thick outside edge, and Dhananjaya de Silva at first slip takes a good catch over his head. Ishan Kishan makes his way back into the hut!
Commentary.Howout: c Dhananjaya de Silva b Dilshan Madushanka

Commentary.Commentary: This one lands down leg, Shubman Gill looks to flick it but gets a rap on his pads and tolls towards the leg side. They cross for a leg bye.
Fuller and on off, Shubman Gill drives it to the man at covers.
On a length, angling in, Ishan Kishan eases it to mid-wicket and scampers through for a single.
Wide! Bowls it slightly shorter and down leg, Ishan Kishan leaves it alone. Starts with a wide ball.

We are all set for the game to begin. The players and the umpires have made their way out in the middle. Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan are the openers for India. Dilshan Madushanka to start with the ball. Here we go...

Rahul Tripathi is in for a quick chat. He says that it is a very special moment for him to represent the country and he feels very happy. Adds that he will look to contribute more and this is a good challenge as this is a series decider. Ends by saying that they can just execute their skills and do their best.

Dasun Shanaka the skipper of Sri Lanka says that they would have batted first as they like to set the tone first. Adds that they focused on the positives and changed the way they played. Ends by saying that Avishka Fernando comes in for Bhanuka Rajapaksa as Avishka has been in good form since LPL and was looking for a spot in the team.

Hardik Pandya the skipper of India says that they will bat first. Adds that the weather is a bit cold and the message for the team was simple, is to play good cricket. Ends by saying that they will go with the same team.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Avishka Fernando (In for Bhanuka Rajapaksa), Charith Asalanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, Dasun Shanaka (C), Wanindu Hasaranga, Chamika Karunaratne, Maheesh Theekshana, Kasun Rajitha, Dilshan Madushanka.

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Ishan Kishan (WK), Shubman Gill, Rahul Tripathi, Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya (C), Deepak Hooda, Axar Patel, Shivam Mavi, Umran Malik, Yuzvendra Chahal, Arshdeep Singh.
TOSS - India have won the toss and will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Kumar Sangakkara is pitchside. He says that there is a greenish tinge of grass which offers the bowlers some assistance. Adds that it's a good pitch to bowl and the toss-winning side will look to bowl first. Ends by saying that it is not a high-scoring pitch and the dew factor is not much here as there hasn't been much in the last two nights.

Sri Lanka have played some exciting cricket in the two games so far but it has been a bit erratic and apart from skipper Dasun Shanaka, no one else has been consistent. The all-rounder has been in magnificent form, especially with the bat and has taken a liking to the Indian pace attack. Unlike the hosts, the Lankan top order did perform well last time around but it is the middle order that needs to step up a bit more. They almost gave it away with the ball in the second game and will be hoping for an improved showing here. Rajkot is a ground famous for run-scoring and the way this series has progressed we might be in for another run-fest. Which side will have the last laugh? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

India were shell-shocked in the last game and their bowlers conceded at a hemmoraghing rate but the spinners and Hardik Pandya bowled pretty well. The inexperienced top order has struggled thus far and it has been the middle order and the all-rounders doing the job with the bat. Axar Patel has been particularly impressive with both bat and ball as he held his nerve with the ball in the first game to win the game and almost won the second game with the bat as well. The hosts will be looking for the top order to deliver here.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 3rd and final T20I between India and Sri Lanka from the Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium in Rajkot. We are locked in for a thrilling final game as the teams are currently level at 1-1 and whoever wins here will win the series as well. In a high-octane clash, it will be interesting to see which side can hold their nerve and be just that bit more clinical.
... MATCH DAY ...

This new year has brought on a rush of cricketing games, giving us hardly any time to catch a breather. Sri Lanka’s tour of India seems to be moving at a brisk rate as we focus our attention on the third and final game of what has been an intriguing T20I series. This game is a decider as both teams have managed to notch up one win under their belt with India looking to maintain their dominance at home and the visitors aspiring to seal a series win on Indian soil for the first time. The first game in Mumbai was a nail-biter in which the hosts won by 2 runs but it could have gone either way. The second game played in Pune saw the Lankans snatch a comfortable 16-run win but they had a bit of a scare toward the end. This game will be played at the Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium in Rajkot and it is to be seen which team goes into the ODI series with the winning momentum. India’s top order has not been good in this series with Ishan Kishan showing glimpses of form in the last game. His opening partner Shubman Gill is having a forgettable series so far and Suryakumar Yadav scored a fighting half-century last time around after failing in the first game. Sanju Samson’s injury paved way for Rahul Tripathi to make his debut and though he was electrifying on the field, he could not make an impact with the bat. The onus of scoring the runs has fallen on their all-rounders Hardik Pandya, Deepak Hooda. and an in-form Axar Patel who has shown some serious hitting ability. Their weakness has been their fast-bowling department which is relatively inexperienced in international cricket but there is no excuse for the number of no balls that were bowled in the previous game. Arshdeep Singh seemed rusty and Shivam Mavi had an off day after an impressive debut in the first fixture where he claimed four wickets. Umran Malik has shown his ability to get the breakthroughs with some searing pace but can be expensive at times. The spinners came back remarkably well in the second game after being carted around all over the field the first time. The Indian coach Rahul Dravid mentioned that they will stick to the same team despite the loss unless there is an injury and that is what is expected. Sri Lanka have been impressive through this series and are giving India a run for their money. Kusal Mendis has been in devastating form but his partner Pathum Nissanka needs to get out of his shell and play freely. Bhanuka Rajapaksa and Dhananjaya de Silva have had a poor series and it is to be seen if the management decides to change things up. Charith Asalanka displayed an array of strokeplay but it is the Sri Lankan skipper Dasun Shanaka who has been a juggernaut for his side in this series with some outstanding hitting chipping in with wickets as well. Kasun Rajitha proved his worth with an outstanding spell of bowling after being dismantled in the earlier game. They have performed as a complete bowling unit with two world-class spinners in Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana chipping in with crucial wickets when required. The pitch in Rajkot has proved to be a batting paradise in the past and we expect loads of runs to be scored in this game. The game will be played at night under clear skies and it will be quite cold under the floodlights. Will India extend their 11-match winning streak in bilateral tournaments? Or will Sri Lanka be able to register their first series win against India away from home? We will find out soon.
